## Scope and relation to the paper

This is a parallel experiment using the zero-shift construction in
`kappa0func.Rmd`. It leaves the original four positive-shift notebooks
unchanged. The equation is
$$
 u_t+\nu(-\Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2}u=f,\qquad\kappa=0,
$$
on the connected tadpole with stem length 1 and loop length 2, with
continuity and Kirchhoff conditions. The fixed geometric gap scale is
$\gamma_*=2/(3\cdot2)=1/3$. It is independent of $h$ and $\tau$ and
introduces no reaction or decay of the constant mode.

The aim is to carry out the smooth and rough convergence studies in
`main.tex`, Section "Numerical experiments", for the unshifted operator.
The zero-shift treatment follows `eq:gamma-scale`, `eq:discrete-means`,
`eq:rational-centered-scheme`, and `thenumericalscheme` in
`Numerical_fractional_diffusion_IMAJNA_kappa0.tex`. Both manuscripts are in
`/home/rierasl/Desktop/6ac76d140751a76e98ae4d0b`.

The necessary operator changes are $L=G$, an exact zero constant eigenvalue,
a positive normalization scale $\gamma_*=1/3$ in place of $\kappa^2$,
and the separate mean update. The convergence data retain their zero mean;
no constants are added to the initial condition or forcing. The separate
nonzero-mean benchmark in the revised paper is a different experiment and
is not substituted for these convergence studies. Meshes, time grids,
error norms, and approximation orders are explicit below; numerical
parameter adjustments must be justified by zero-shift error-budget checks.
Internal diagnostics belong to `DOCS/NAP`, outside this report.

The computed zero-shift errors and slopes are new results for the
unshifted equation. They are not expected to equal the positive-shift
numbers in `main.tex`, because the modal rates change from
$\nu(\mu_j+16)^{\alpha/2}$ to $\nu\mu_j^{\alpha/2}$.

## Running and knitting

This notebook follows the original experiment workflow. All full-run
parameters are explicit in the parameter chunk below. There are no
validation profiles or global options that select a different experiment.

1. Run the setup and parameter chunks in RStudio.
2. Run the computation chunk manually to generate `true_diff_conv_in_tau_mat_paper.rds`.
3. Knit the notebook to load that saved result, print its tables, and draw
   its plots. Knitting never advances a PDE solution, compiles a solver,
   or runs internal tests. Missing or incompatible results stop with an
   instruction to run the computation chunk.

Use the R installation containing `rSPDE`, `Matrix`, `Rcpp`, and
`RcppEigen` for computation (for example `/usr/bin/Rscript`). Knitting
needs the reporting packages only. Internal implementation tests and
refinement studies are kept separately in
`/home/rierasl/Desktop/DOCS/NAP/true_diff_internal`.

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,error=FALSE,cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png",fig.width=8,fig.height=5)
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2",quietly=TRUE)) stop("Install ggplot2 to render the plots.")
```

## Parameters

These are the full experiment settings. Edit them here before running
the computation. `workers` controls execution only; it does not change
the mathematical problem. The `_paper` filename suffix is retained for
compatibility with previously generated full-run results.

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-parameters}
T_final <- 1
kappa <- 0
gamma_star <- 1/3
alpha_vector <- seq(0.9,1.7,0.1)
diffusion <- 1e-3
h_fixed <- 1e-3
tau_vector <- T_final/c(200L,63L,20L,6L,2L)
m_fixed <- 8L
overkill_h <- 1e-5
overkill_time_step <- 1e-5
workers <- 9L
K <- 16L
initial_modes <- c(5L,6L,8:21)
initial_amplitude <- 10
forcing_amplitude <- 10
initial_mean <- 0
forcing_mean <- 0
AAA <- 1
OMEGA <- pi
stopifnot(length(initial_modes)==K,!(7L %in% initial_modes))
output_file <- "data_files/true_diff_conv_in_tau_mat_paper.rds"

# Bundle only the visible parameters above for the shared runner.
settings <- list(study="tau",T_final=T_final,kappa=kappa,gamma_star=gamma_star,
    alpha=alpha_vector,diffusion=diffusion,workers=workers,initial_modes=initial_modes,
    initial_amplitude=initial_amplitude,forcing_amplitude=forcing_amplitude,
    initial_mean=initial_mean,forcing_mean=forcing_mean,A=AAA,omega=OMEGA,h=h_fixed,tau=tau_vector,m=m_fixed,
    reference_h=overkill_h,reference_tau=overkill_time_step)
settings_table <- data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1)))
knitr::kable(settings_table)
```

## Data, projection, and exact continuous reference

Keep the original smooth experiment's normalized eigenfunctions, with
$\mathcal J=\{5,6,8,\ldots,21\}$, $K=16$, and use
$$
 u_0=\frac{a_0}{\sqrt K}\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}e_j,
 \qquad f(s,t)=a_f A\sin(\omega t)e_7(s).
$$
As in `main.tex`, $a_0=a_f=10$, $A=1$, $\omega=\pi$, and
both spatial means are zero. Thus $\|u_0\|_{L_2}=10$ and $M(t)=0$.
The visible `initial_mean` and `forcing_mean` parameters are both zero;
they must remain zero for this mean-zero convergence experiment. The
general solver still handles its constant mode exactly, including any
roundoff residual. Nonzero-mean tests are kept separately in `DOCS/NAP`.

The mode table is defined in `kappa0_mode_table()`: $e_1=1/\sqrt3$,
$e_5=\phi_3$, $e_7=\psi_4$, with unshifted eigenvalues
$\mu_j=(k_j\pi/2)^2$. For a positive mode and
$d_j=\nu\mu_j^{\alpha/2}$, its exact coefficient is
$$
 a_j(t)=a_j(0)e^{-d_jt}+b_jA
       \int_0^t e^{-d_j(t-s)}\sin(\omega s)\,ds.
$$
`kappa0_decayed_sine_convolution()` evaluates the convolution stably near
$t=0$. The reference retains exactly the 17 active positive modes and has no
constant component. Continuous eigenfunctions are used to specify data
and evaluate the reference, not as a truncation of the numerical solver.

`kappa0_smooth_data()` assembles sine/cosine-hat loads analytically and
solves the consistent mass system for $P_hu_0$. The time forcing uses
its exact interval average, evaluated with a midpoint-sinc formula.
At each step the solver forms
$$
 v=CU^k+\tau F_{\rm sine}\overline g_{k+1},
 \quad q=\mathbf1^Tv/3,\quad b=v-qC\mathbf1.
$$
It applies the cached sparse rational update to $b$ and returns the
centered coefficients plus $q\mathbf1$. The mean recurrence and its
code mapping are documented in Section 4.1 of `kappa0func.Rmd`.

## Space-time error and reconstruction

For $t\in(t_{k-1},t_k]$, use the right-constant reconstruction
$\widetilde U(t)=U^k$. On a fixed reference mesh with consistent mass
$C_\star$, let $\Psi$ evaluate the solver hats at reference nodes.
The reported quantity is
$$
 E^2=\tau_\star\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_\star}
 [u_{\rm ref}(t_\ell^\star)-\Psi U^{k(\ell)}]^T C_\star
 [u_{\rm ref}(t_\ell^\star)-\Psi U^{k(\ell)}],
 \quad t_\ell^\star\in(t_{k(\ell)-1},t_{k(\ell)}].
$$
This is the same sampled norm as the original notebook. The reference
is evaluated analytically; no fine-grid reference PDE is solved.
`kappa0_prepare_reference_error()` compresses this quadratic form into
its coarse metric, reference projection, and residual Gram matrix.
The compiled kernel groups coefficient samples belonging to the same
solver interval and accumulates their weighted means and centered
scatter. This computes the sampled sum without storing all reference
vectors or subtracting nearly equal norm squares. It is not exact
continuum integration in space or time.

Every solver step is advanced. Mass is checked at every step, not only
at reference samples. The exact constant component is zero, so there is no added uniform
forcing or constant-mode reconstruction error. The positive-mode temporal
reconstruction error remains part of this space-time norm. Spatial and temporal reference refinement, rational-order
refinement, and solver-time refinement should be used when errors
approach a floor; implementation agreement alone does not certify these
separate discretization budgets.

## Temporal convergence and interpretation

Vary $\tau=T/N$ with $N\in\{200,63,20,6,2\}$ while fixing $h$ and
$m$. Backward Euler has reference slope 1, so fit
$\log E=s_\tau\log\tau+b$. The full experiment uses $h=10^{-3}$,
$\nu=10^{-3}$ and reference resolutions $10^{-5}$, with rational order
8, as in `main.tex`. At the smallest tau and the tested endpoint exponents
0.9 and 1.7, changing order 8 to order 14 changed the measured error by
at most 0.003%. The internal comparison is in
`DOCS/NAP/true_diff_internal/mean_zero_order_audit.csv`.
The settings are printed above; positive-shift saved errors are never loaded.

For each time grid, recompute the exact interval forcing averages and
all time-step poles, residues, and shifted factorizations. Their strength
is $\tau\nu\gamma_*^{\alpha/2}$, so an operator cached for another
$\tau$ cannot be reused. The sampled continuum comparison includes the
right-constant reconstruction error. Both exact and discrete spatial means are zero (up to roundoff); no
increasing uniform mean is added to the temporal error. It is therefore different from the paper's
independent final-time comparison with exact semidiscrete evolution.

## Computation

Run this chunk manually after the setup and parameters. `eval=FALSE`
prevents it from running when knitting. This explicit action computes
the experiment and overwrites only the named full-run result file.
It does not run internal implementation tests or refinement studies.

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-recompute, eval=FALSE}
for (package in c("Matrix","rSPDE","Rcpp","RcppEigen"))
    if (!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
true_diff <- local({
    extracted <- tempfile("true_diff_functions_",fileext=".R")
    on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
    knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
    functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
    sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
    functions
})
result <- true_diff$kappa0_compute_study(settings,"true_diff_conv_in_tau_mat.Rmd",output_file)
```

## Load saved results

This is the only experiment-data action taken while knitting. Check the
saved scientific parameters against the visible settings. A worker-count
change does not invalidate numerical results. Historical internal-check
fields, if present in an older result, are not executed or displayed.
Source hashes and package versions are retained as provenance; source
changes do not silently launch another computation.

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-load-results}
if (!file.exists(output_file))
    stop("Saved results are missing: ",output_file,
         ". Run the setup, parameters, and recompute chunks manually, then knit.")
result <- readRDS(output_file)
scientific_parameters <- setdiff(names(settings),"workers")
mismatch <- scientific_parameters[!vapply(scientific_parameters,function(name)
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$parameters[[name]],settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if (length(mismatch))
    stop("Saved settings differ for: ",paste(mismatch,collapse=", "),
         ". Run the recompute chunk manually for these parameters, then knit.")
cat("Generated:",result$generated_at,"\nSaved computation seconds:",
    round(result$elapsed_seconds,2),"\nSaved worker count:",result$parameters$workers,"\n")
```

## Results and fitted rates

The benchmark slopes describe the theoretical rate scale. The observed
fits use the computed data below; they are not replaced by the benchmark.
For smooth data, `max_mass_error` is the maximum absolute discrepancy from
the discrete mass recurrence over the entire trajectory. For the rough
reduction the full-graph mass is zero by symmetry, validated independently.

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-rates}
knitr::kable(result$rates,digits=6)
```

```{r true-diff-conv-in-tau-mat-plot-results}
d <- result$results
d$alpha_label <- factor(d$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
if (settings$study=="m") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape=resolved))+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time L2 error",
            colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",title="Zero-shift rational convergence")
} else {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x=if(settings$study=="tau") "tau" else "h",
            y="Sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha",title="Zero-shift convergence")
}
# Reference curves retain their prescribed slope and are geometrically
# anchored to the data. They are guides, not additional computed errors.
guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    power <- if(settings$study=="m") -2*pi*sqrt(a/2) else if(settings$study=="tau") 1 else 2
    xx <- if(settings$study=="m") sqrt(x$m) else log(x$axis)
    if(settings$study=="rough_h") power <- a
    x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$error)-power*xx)+power*xx)
    x
}))
guides$alpha_label <- factor(guides$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
p <- p+ggplot2::geom_line(data=guides,ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)+ggplot2::labs(subtitle=sprintf("kappa=0; gamma*=%g",settings$gamma_star))
print(p)
figure_dir <- "data_files/true_diff_conv_in_tau_mat_paper"
dir.create(figure_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"convergence.pdf"),p,width=8,height=5)
```
